article_annotations.title: China ready to offer assistance after Indonesia earthquake
article_annotations.source_independence_reason: 新华社电头，报道中国外交部例行记者会。
article_annotations.content:
BEIJING, Aug. 17 (Xinhua) -- China is concerned about the earthquake in Indonesia and is ready to provide assistance in accordance with Indonesia's needs, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Monday.

"We express our deep condolences to the victims and sincere sympathies to the families of the deceased and the injured," Lin said at a daily media briefing in response to the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck Flores Island, Indonesia, on Aug. 15.

It is understood that some Chinese citizens have been injured in the earthquake, Lin said, adding that the Chinese Consulate General in Denpasar has activated its emergency mechanism to provide assistance to those affected.

article_annotations.title: Powerful aftershock hits Indonesian communities still waiting for aid as earthquake death toll rises to 68
article_annotations.source_independence_reason: Yahoo 承载的正文引述 AP 对 Reo 居民的采访，与 A003 的引语和细节有重合，完整稿源未确认。
article_annotations.content:
The death toll from Saturday's earthquake in Indonesia has risen to at least ‌68, as powerful aftershocks continued to strike fear into communities on the island of Flores where thousands of people are still waiting for aid .

A magnitude-5.9 tremor was recorded at a depth of about 10km by Germany 's GFZ Research Centre for Geosciences on Monday, though there were no immediate reports of further casualties.

The agency has recorded at least 995 aftershocks since Saturday, 46 of which were powerful enough to be felt by residents. The strongest before Monday's measured 6.2.

Indonesia on Monday marked its 81st Independence Day, which residents of Flores spent mourning, searching for relatives and waiting for supplies to reach them.

President Prabowo Subianto asked the nation to pray for people affected by the disaster in East Nusa Tenggara and other parts of the country, as well as leading a nationwide moment of silence honouring Indonesia's independence heroes.

The province's governor declared a 14-day state of emergency on Sunday, with the earthquake death toll continuing to climb as rescue teams work through debris. Officials expect it to rise further as they reach more villages cut off by landslides. Most of the deaths were recorded in the districts of Sikka, Manggarai and East Manggarai.

The magnitude-7.7 earthquake that struck on Saturday morning had its epicentre about 68km north-west of Ende, a town on the south coast of Flores, according to the US Geological Survey.

Flores lies in East Nusa Tenggara, a province of scattered islands at the eastern end of the Indonesian archipelago.

At least 200 people were injured and more than 2,000 homes were damaged across East Nusa Tenggara province, nearly 250 of them destroyed on Flores alone, the National Disaster Management Agency said. About 5,000 people are in temporary shelters.

Villagers rest in a tent on an open field in Marapokot, Nagekeo, East Nusa Tenggara (AFP/Getty)

Thousands more spent Sunday night under tarpaulins beside their collapsed houses rather than risk going indoors.

More than 3,500 military and police personnel have been deployed and 275 tonnes of aid sent into the disaster zone, but the terrain has slowed deliveries to the worst-affected communities.

"We are continuing to collect reports of damage and casualties, but there are communication disruptions," said the East Nusa Tenggara police chief, Rudi Darmoko, who described severe structural damage and collapsed buildings, with power cuts hampering communications.

Landslides have blocked sections of the Trans-Flores highway in Ende regency, the road that runs about 435 miles across the island from Labuan Bajo to Larantuka. Rescue officials have warned the death toll could rise, with villages across six regencies buried or cut off, and the disaster agency has sent a helicopter to carry supplies and support possible evacuations.

"My house is just rubble now," Rasyid Jafar, a clothing trader in the village of Reo, the worst-hit part of Manggarai regency, told the Associated Press. "We need food, medicine and clean water urgently."

Survivors say what has arrived is not enough to live on. "We have nothing left. Why isn't there a public kitchen?" Mariana Tewu, another Reo villager, told the news agency.

Local television showed patients being wheeled out of several hospitals as a precaution, with staff moving beds and oxygen cylinders outside and setting up temporary treatment areas.

Saturday's quake prompted a tsunami warning and sent coastal residents to higher ground before it was lifted when no significant change in sea levels was detected. Flores was struck by a tsunami after an earthquake in 1992 that killed about 2,500 people.

Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, the belt of seismic activity around the edges of the ocean, and records frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. An earthquake on Sulawesi in 2018 killed more than 4,400 people, and the magnitude 9.1 quake off Sumatra in 2004 caused a tsunami that killed about 230,000 people across a dozen countries.

article_annotations.title: Thousands in Indonesia await aid after quake kills 68, overshadowing Independence Day
article_annotations.source_independence_reason: NewsNow 承载稿含 REO 电头，与 A002 明示来自 AP 的现场引语一致，完整署名未保留。
article_annotations.content:
REO, Indonesia — Thousands of people waited for aid on the Indonesian island of Flores on Monday (Aug 17) as the country marked its 81st Independence Day, two days after a powerful earthquake killed at least 68 people, injured more than 200 others and damaged thousands of homes.

Many residents on Flores island in East Nusa Tenggara province spent the day mourning victims while military teams tried to deliver food, clean water and clothing to inaccessible communities by plane.

The Saturday morning quake left widespread damage, with buildings collapsed onto parked cars, homes shattered and trees and boulders blocking roads.

"My house is just rubble now," said Rasyid Jafar, a clothing trader in the village of Reo, the hardest-hit area in Manggarai regency. "We need food, medicine and clean water urgently."

During Indonesia's Independence Day ceremony in the capital, Jakarta, President Prabowo Subianto asked participants to pray for people affected by disasters in East Nusa Tenggara and other parts of the country, while leading a nationwide moment of silence honoring the nation's independence heroes.

More than 4,500 homes were damaged when the quake struck Flores island early Saturday. Some 19,000 people were forced into temporary shelters and 213 people were injured, according to the National Disaster Management Agency or BNPB.

The disaster also damaged 122 health facilities, 252 schools and 84 places of worship.

The province's governor declared a 14-day state of emergency on Sunday.

The quake occurred at a depth of 10 kilometres shortly before 6am (7am SGT) Saturday, according to the US Geological Survey, and residents fled in panic as tsunami warnings were issued but later lifted.

Authorities have since recorded 1,576 aftershocks into Monday, though only 54 were felt by residents.

Thousands of people on Flores camped outside collapsed homes under tarpaulin tents overnight into Monday, sleeping outside because of the danger of more aftershocks.

For many residents, the disaster revived painful memories of a powerful earthquake and tsunami that struck Flores in 1992, killing about 2,500 people.

As thousands of survivors remain in need of food, shelter and medical treatment, the government said more than 1,800 military and police personnel have been deployed across the disaster zone, supported by 10 aircraft and several vessels, to distribute more than 100 metric tons of emergency aid.

Nearly 5,400 food packages, two field hospital tents, medicines and clothing were being delivered to communities across the disaster zone, as logistical challenges slowed deliveries to some hard-hit communities, national disaster agency Deputy Chief Abdul Muhari said in a video statement.

Authorities set up two emergency field hospitals in the worst-hit town of Ruteng to treat earthquake victims after local hospitals were damaged, with two crisis management teams overseeing a health emergency operation centre, Muhari said.

He also said rescue teams continued searching for victims in the affected areas, although no residents have reported any family members still missing.

Aid workers reached tiny Palue Island, one of the areas closest to the earthquake's epicentre, late Sunday, after a difficult sea and land journey through landslide-hit terrain, authorities said. Thousands of residents remained in urgent need of assistance.

"The roads are steep and many were blocked by landslides. It was a near-death journey," said the deputy police chief of Sikka regency, Marselus Yugo Amboro, whose team was among the first to reach the island with emergency supplies.

He said initial assessments revealed extensive damage, with one villager killed, two seriously injured and nearly 150 homes destroyed.

Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, is prone to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions because of its location on the Pacific "Ring of Fire", a horseshoe-shaped arc of seismic faults and volcanoes.

In 2018, a magnitude 7.5 earthquake triggered a tsunami on the island of Sulawesi that killed more than 4,400 people. In 2004, a magnitude 9.1 quake off Sumatra unleashed a tsunami that killed about 230,000 people in a dozen countries, nearly 170,000 in Aceh province alone.
